reviews.text: As fanciful notions play out against implausible situations, it's hard to shake the feeling that it's a little too clever for its own good. That said, Glass Onion is an easy, entertaining, if increasingly convoluted, watch.
reviews.author: Karl Puschmann

reviews.text: The protagonists may make you recoil in disgust but the film itself is ultimately plenty of fun.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Stands on its own as a great movie that continues what we love about the original without retreading or losing what made it so fresh.
reviews.author: Joseph Tomastik

reviews.text: Towards the end of the film, Blanc, annoyed and full of fervor, declares that it’s “all so dumb.” I couldn’t help but wonder if he, right there in that moment, could somehow read my mind.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: Like the glass onion atop Miles’ vacation home, the Knives Out sequel is both intricately layered and deceptively simple.
reviews.author: Ally Ham

reviews.text: Even when it’s building up its characters prior to the murder, Johnson’s direction ensures that the suspenseful, adrenaline charged tone attributed to rollercoasters is always present.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: A truly theatrical experience that will make you laugh, gasp, cheer, and remember how exciting cinema can be.
reviews.author: Jericho Tadeo

reviews.text: A carefully constructed mystery that probes at the twisted way our basic modes of interacting with each other have become distorted.
reviews.author: Joshua Polanski

reviews.text: It’s difficult to make a really good, original mystery film, but to do it twice, within three years of each other? Incredible.
reviews.author: Zach Youngs

reviews.text: Whatever you expect from Glass Onion, Johnson delivers in a way that’s wholly unexpected, yet never anything but delightful.
reviews.author: Joonatan Itkonen

reviews.text: You could fully skip this movie or watch it…it doesn’t matter. Go watch The Last of Shelia
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: If it has to be 3 hours long, write a better script
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: Glass Onion is another fantastic whodunnit from Rian Johnson, but is it better than Knives Out? Well, that comes down to personal preference and what you seek from these films.
reviews.author: Amy Smith

reviews.text: This movie, unsurprisingly, is incredibly smart, and probably a tad more subtle than its predecessor.
reviews.author: Dave Giannini

reviews.text: While there are elements of the film that stand out as compelling, the mystery at the core is not one of them.
reviews.author: Wesley Lovell

reviews.text: There are enough twists and turns in Rian Johnson’s Knives Out follow-up to keep sharp-eyed viewers of all kinds happy, and the location is the best kind of eye candy.
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: This is the Aliens of the Knives Out universe, an exponential iteration of a great concept that by now knows its lead character inside out and is thinking big when it comes to finding a cerebral challenge that is worthy of him.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: Just like its predecessor, Johnson lashes out at everyone and points out the absurdity and stupidity of the rich and powerful by embodying the caricatures of real-life people.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: Overall, the movie is more playful than serious, and its dedication to slowly solving the puzzle makes it both dizzying and delightful.
reviews.author: Lee Zumpe

reviews.text: Glass Onion isn’t just a film — it’s a masterfully crafted game that somehow grows more fun the more you play it, allowing you to pick up on small but rich details you didn’t initially spot.
reviews.author: Taylor Gates

reviews.text: “Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery” is more of a madcap film than “Knives Out,” piling on the absurdity from the opening credits. And just like the 2019 version, the cast is its biggest strength.
reviews.author: Kevin Slane

reviews.text: A standard murder mystery elevated by a very talented cast.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: If lacking in the surprise factor of Knives Out, Glass Onion is a riotous time, dialling up the laughs and mystery with cameos and surprises galore, and layers of clever dialogue and writing.
reviews.author: Christopher Connor

reviews.text: So, all told, I honestly can't quite rate Glass Onion quite as high as I did Knives Out, but it's still tremendous fun with Rian Johnson once again proving just why the murder mystery genre is such an enduring – if sometimes neglected – crowd favourite.
reviews.author: Ilan Preskovsky

reviews.text: While Daniel Craig's Benoit Blanc is obviously the star of Glass Onion, it's Janelle Monáe and Kate Hudson that really shine.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: Is bigger and more lavish, with moments of big-budget lushness sharply delivered by director Rian Johnson... that doesn’t amount to a better project.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: Thank you Daniel Craig for leaving Bond to give us more Benoit Blanc!
reviews.author: Jillian Chilingerian

reviews.text: Better than the first Knives Out. An incredible mystery that had me all the way up to every single reveal. Rian johnson you genius! Literally hanging on every single word/sequence.
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Unlike other franchises that seemingly stick around far longer than they’re welcome, the mysteries of Benoit Blanc have the potential to delight for years to come.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is a perfect sequel—it’s sharp, meticulously striking, and bold, with a mindful excavation of elitism and the lengths people go through to maintain their dominion.
reviews.author: Gissane Sophia

reviews.text: Johnson replaces the insular familial privilege at the heart of Knives Out with an even more obnoxious form of privilege whose odiousness is in direct proportion to how much its characters flaunt it in the public sphere
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Glass Onion flexes the durability of Johnson's twist on a classic genre formula and the adaptability of its central sleuth.
reviews.author: Eric Webb

reviews.text: Rian Johnson's knife is sharper and more precise the second time out.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: Rian Johnson’s Knives Out (2019) was a delightful surprise, and now Netflix has thrown tons of money at a semi-sequel, and too much money has ruined the concept.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: Janelle Monae, the other lead, is seventy times more magnetic than Ana De Armas was in the last film...
reviews.author: Elissa Suh

reviews.text: The director managed to perfectly thread the needle, ensuring that ‘Glass Onion’ felt unique but still delighted the fans of its predecessor.
reviews.author: Daniel Joyaux

reviews.text: Johnson's second crack at his franchise is a worthy successor to the Knives Out name that dangles suspense overhead - but not without setting the standards for the modern murder-mystery movie.
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: This hilarious and intricately-plotted ‘Knives Out’ sequel is just as fun as the original —even if some of the characters and social satire don’t pack quite the same punch.
reviews.author: Gavia Baker-Whitelaw

reviews.text: Reteaming Johnson with actor Daniel Craig as genteel master detective Benoit Blanc, it is a smart storytelling treat — and also the rare sequel that fully lives up to its promise.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: It is Janelle Monae who hits it far out like Ana de Armas in Knives Out when Johnson suddenly pulls the rabbit out of the hat in his super fun twisting and turning that tops the first film by far.
reviews.author: Brian Susbielles

reviews.text: The lack of regulations, the extreme wealth, and the few scruples of this particular class of nouveau riche is the background of this satire, which, although superficial, has a massive reach and leaves us questioning the facts. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: Craig and Monae have the most fun and give easily the best performances. When they’re together on screen, it’s as if they are aloof to the rest of the movie and cast. The rest of the movie, though, tries so hard to top the sizzle of the original.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: This is a rich, perfectly orchestrated performance that could have gone wrong even with the slightest of misjudgement in character. That her performance gets even better in the second watch...
reviews.author: Santanu Das

reviews.text: All the money in the world, and “Glass Onion” never feels meaningfully engaged in any aesthetically definitive approach to a mystery instead it is overwhelmed by a strangely incurious approach to the people, the locales and itself.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: It seems to me an enjoyable, solvent sequel, whose surprise factor is as sharp as a piece of glass. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Like Knives Out, Glass Onion fronts as a frothy potboiler just out for a good time. But in its heart, it’s a scathing satire of our oligarchic ruling class.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: Benoit Blanc’s return to the big screen brings with it another superb Rian Johnson whodunit, that seriously rivals the original Knives Out mystery.
reviews.author: Hamish Calvert

reviews.text: Both 'Glass Onion' and 'The Menu' owe some of their success and much of our enjoyment to the late, great Lady Mallowan. We are deep into Agatha Christie territory here.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: For all of the great satire of (GLASS ONION), the true brilliance of Rian Johnson's scrip, is that it creates this facade that suggests something deeper as it relates to Billionaire power and how they continue to create influence.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: Case solved and justice dispensed in bizarre, spectacular, and unconvincing ways. It is an entertaining and amusing movie, but a step down from its immediate predecessor.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Linearly plotted, Glass Onion is stunningly unfunny and desperately wacky; a barely coherent mess moved by a silly game with no thrills and no real mystery.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Suffers from sequel-itus: you hope for something better but you get something a little less.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: There’s something undeniably soothing about gathering everyone in the drawing room — or the 2020s equivalent of a drawing room — and wrapping everything up in a bright bow of clear explication and unequivocal justice.
reviews.author: Alison Gillmor

reviews.text: A collage of small, clever, lovingly shaped skits struggling to join the narrative stream of a single story. Albeit with some of the best cameos in the business. Inevitably, it ends up riding the coattails of its stellar predecessor.
reviews.author: Milana Vujkov

reviews.text: A murder mystery can provide sharp social commentary—and great fun.
reviews.author: Kathryn Reklis

reviews.text: Glass Onion is a charming, funny, and impeccably made film that is as breezy as it is clever. The script is the star of the show, with delectable lines worthy of a second (or third) viewing, and a perfectly balanced cast that delivers with gusto.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: This franchise is shaping up to be a perfect delight.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: A fun, charismatic round of "Clue" with impressive technical components that doesn't quite round off due to high levels of self-awareness that work both against and in favor of the film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nilton Arana

reviews.text: The men and women of Glass Onion reach equality numbers-wise, but it’s the women who receive more interesting backstories, more satisfying story arcs, and more enviable wardrobes to boot.
reviews.author: Symphony Barnes

reviews.text: While the pieces are there for a fascinating puzzle, the final product is an overstuffed film that doesn’t have the same satirical smarts as the first.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: Glass Onion is either too smart or too lazy; I’m not sure which.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Writer-director Rian Johnson has delivered a pleasing potpourri that’s peppered with wordplay and is blended with some strong characters who rescue the film from its lesser elements.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Benoit Blanc (Daniel Craig, never mind his accent), a dapper Columbo, a sunny locale, striking set design, a well-written screenplay and seamless editing, and not least, an animated ensemble cast, we get an entertaining feature.
reviews.author: Diana Cheng

reviews.text: "One of the most purely pleasurable movies of the year."
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: Glass Onion isn’t as lavish or tricky but it is definitely twisty and makes for an entertaining watch.
reviews.author: Renuka Vyavahare

reviews.text: The Benoit Blanc cinematic universe is superior and I hope it never ends.
reviews.author: Steph Cozza

reviews.text: Silly, showy, sybaritic sequel...
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Rian Johnson creates another clever whodunit in the form of the Knives Out sequel Glass Onion.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: Seldom has a film boasted more glass statuary. As the credits roll, you can’t help but expect a thank you to the manufacturers of Windex.
reviews.author: Brandon Judell

reviews.text: A riotous, twisty good time with high energy, outstanding performances, and a brilliantly balanced script that is clever, smart, and often outright hilarious.
reviews.author: Aaron White

reviews.text: A delightfully entertaining romp!
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: As much as I want to see Johnson explore and expand his talent to other genres and themes,  I would not be dissatisfied if he spent the rest of his career creating new mysteries for Benoit Blanc. [Full review in Portuguese]
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: ...a romp reminiscent of the splashy, all-star Agatha Christie adaptations of yore, like Death on the Nile (1978), and if Johnson steals shamelessly from the Queen of Crime, at least he’s stealing from the best.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: It’s the kind of movie that persuades many people they’re having a good time because it keeps telling them they are, with nudge-nudge, wink-wink cavorting from performers whose forte is not comedy.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Every step in the mechanism is designed to make an obvious point about abuse of power and self-involved excess. Yet, after all has been revealed, we realize that there was absolutely no reason for the whole contraption to get started in the first place.
reviews.author: Ethan Iverson

reviews.text: As a revenge movie this would work, but as a murder mystery it splutters back and forth across a clunky and confused narrative. We wanted Benoit Blanc at his best, but instead got a bland B-list amateur solving a different case entirely.
reviews.author: Ben Turner

reviews.text: The most fun I had at the movies in 2022.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: “Glass Onion” is a fun puzzle box that’s preposterous fun — no more, no less. It's a blast until it isn’t, but even if the reveal doesn't work, it's pretty damn fun getting there.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: Proof that filmmaking is a thing of the past, "Glass Onion" is a tone-deaf crime comedy whose overblown budget would have been better spent on New York City's infrastructure.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Glass Onion is a well-made, multilayered murder mystery, whose appeal lies not only in its subversive story but in its prescient ability to predict the future. It's one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: David Fontana

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is one of the best films of 2022 because it reminds you just how fun the movies can be.
reviews.author: Diandra Reviews

reviews.text: A standalone sequel to Knives Out is here, and it's even better than the first Benoit Blanc outing.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: It’s a high-end game – a marble chess set.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: Hauls itself up to a bleary-eyed 139-minute running time to cover about 85 minutes worth of story.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: A deliciously twisty remix of the classic British-style murder mystery, with a fabulous location and a group of suspects who all have motive and opportunity. Also like its predecessor, it has an all-star cast clearly enjoying themselves enormously.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Glass Onion and Knives Out are so good, I'm ready to forgive Rian Johnson for The Last Jedi. This is where the healing begins.
reviews.author: Adam Olinger

reviews.text: Everyone will find something to enjoy and come out of it excited for more of Benoit Blanc’s sharp retort and quick-witted sleuthing.
reviews.author: Zofia Wijaszka

reviews.text: Glass Onion is bigger and slightly glossier than its predecessor. While  the mystery is slight, the comedy and performances are great, particularly Monae and Hudson. Queer rep is iffy, but for audiences who liked Knives Out, this is catnip.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: I enjoyed Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery well enough. It’s diverting entertainment, although its 139 minute running time is 20 minutes too long and it takes too much time to get the plot in motion.
reviews.author: Niall Browne

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery has broad characters, stale soap opera tropes, and a subplot straight out of a Tyler Perry movie - yet, somehow, Rian Johnson pulls it all off.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Johnson has traded out box office cash for streaming revenue in a Netflix-exclusive sequel that both improves on its predecessor yet also falls short in different ways.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Unlike onions, this movie lacks layers, but it's not lacking in fun. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro Alemán

reviews.text: Please keep the Benoit Blanc Cinematic Universe going as long as possible.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: Glass Onion takes audiences on the same journey as Blanc himself, misdirecting us beautifully and making you intentionally overthink the story... when at heart, the nature of this particular mystery is something far more ridiculous.
reviews.author: Jack Bottomley

reviews.text: A well-composed and sharply delivered sequel that seamlessly builds upon the foundation of its acclaimed predecessor.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Glass Onion is a perfect reminder that great art need not be serious. Sometimes, it’s just about having fun. If you look closely, even the Mona Lisa is smiling just a little.
reviews.author: David Mack

reviews.text: Blanc is bland, and despite all its bells and whistles, so is the movie.
reviews.author: Shubhra Gupta

reviews.text: Sequel to one of the best murder mystery stories in past few years, this finds ways  supersedes what’s come before it. The cast, the script, the environment, are all double the amount of engagement & intrigued. Monáe has an amazing performance here! GREAT
reviews.author: Samuel Leggett Jr.

reviews.text: Now playing the sharp Southern sleuth for the second time, Daniel Craig is as smooth as a craft cocktail at a swanky soiree. He oozes smarts and charm, carrying the film with much authority.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Glass Onion does not knock it out of the park mystery-wise, nor is the dialogue on its predecessor's level, and the cast also lack cohesion. Still, the overarching themes of wealth, privilege, and just desserts always entertains.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: Johnson’s plotting isn’t quite as tight as in the previous outing, but the laughs are just as big and the schadenfreude is too frothy not to let it fizz delightfully on our lips.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: If the much-touted “Christie scheme” can feel overdone at times, Johnson and his ensemble turn it into a contagious exercise of wit, precision, and playfulness. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: 'Glass Onion' is a delicious murder mystery in which Rian Johnson once again gives that cosy feeling of Christie's tales, and at the same time gives his own subversive touch.
reviews.author: Kshitij Rawat

reviews.text: Glass Onion is one of the great whodunnits, a scintillating piece of work that includes all the best aspects of the genre: death, mystery, comedy and revenge.
reviews.author: Asher Luberto

reviews.text: It’s not much of a mystery. But sure is fun getting to where you know you’re going, thanks to a handful of clever twists and an abundance of sharp-witted dialogue poking fun at the loathsomeness of the sycophants among the upper one percent.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: ... Benoit Blanc goes full Hercule Poirot... fun but feels more intent on whimsy than trudging up anything sinister... the preachy commentary holds the sequel down from reaching the heights of its predecessor.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Thanks to Cline's quick wit and suspicious nature, Whiskey is a stand-out in the ensemble movie.
reviews.author: Fletcher Peters

reviews.text: I thoroughly enjoyed Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery. I loved the mystery. I laughed, had a good time, and can’t wait to watch it again.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: [The story] lost its Agatha Christie-sque elegance by embracing Columbo-like broad strokes. Yet, the Brit [Daniel Craig] is such a good actor that he comes out winning even when the script demands less subtlety for humor's sake. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillermo Courau

reviews.text: Glass Onion works best as a bitter critique of contemporary foolishness in all its splendor than as a criminal intrigue. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Story swings bigger than the last film and somehow feels more poignant.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: The twisty plot isn't quite as ingenious as Johnson's last one, but the writer-director has gone all-out to make everything in Glass Onion as big, broad, funny and colourful as Daniel Craig's southern drawl.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: For Round Two with Benoit Blanc, Johnson feels far more confident in this world, willing to take risks and experiment with whodunnit conventions to a much greater extent than he did three years ago.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: It's even funnier as the plot crashes through its crazy twists and turns, subverting the mystery genre itself before giving in to its more enjoyable pleasures: make everyone a suspect before unpeeling a satisfyingly thumping conclusion.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: ...a briskly-paced and perpetually unpredictable endeavor...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: ... it never feels excessive or heavy, neither does it feel excessively light. [Rian Johnson] has magically found the exact sweet spot without sacrificing complexity. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: The humor upholds and instead of twists and shouts, Glass Onion delivers twists and murders. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: While not quite as clever as the first Knives Out movie from 2019, sharp lines, smart twists and lively performances suggest a bright future for Craig’s detective Benoit Blanc.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: It’s clever, witty, and engrossing, and pays tribute to the inherent novelty and menace of its predecessor while giving its hero something new...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: This is a bigger, fancier, and more complex escapade, while maintaining Johnson’s playful spirit and keen eye for social commentary.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: A film that feels less fresh than its predecessor, and that certainly has some structural issues that distracted me, but that still works to make us fall even more in love with Benoit Blanc. Full review in Spanish. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: This is simply not a good story, and Johnson struggles to draw the necessary emotional component from these friends and their difficult relationships. There’s conflict but no feeling.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: The story lacks tension and reason. It is slow, even boring. The dialogue is uninspiring. The denouement is ridiculous and unfulfilling. If Benoit was the “world’s greatest detective” before, now he isn’t in the top 100. Hercule Poirot needn't worry.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: More playful than its predecessor but still as socially relevant, Rian Johnson’s Netflix film finds Daniel Craig in particularly debonair form.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Although Johnson’s reach slightly exceeds his grasp here, it’s extremely easy to recommend something as multi-faceted as Glass Onion. It has comedy, drama, action, mystery, and almost a dozen fantastic performances full of charm and charisma.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: An original and extremely satisfying whodunit that entertains from start to finish through the organic conjunction of its narrative, acting, and technical elements. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: Rian Johnson is really getting the hang of this Agatha Christie thing.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Glass Onion is saturated with enchanting moments and quick-witted dialogue, along with Janelle Monáe’s wonderful performance as Bron’s estranged best friend...
reviews.author: Maxwell Rabb

reviews.text: Johnson (and Netflix) have a hit on their hands and lucky for us, there are two more in the pike. On a cold winter’s night, there’s nothing better to warm your heart than a good old-fashioned murder mystery filled with intrigue and laughter.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: Glass Onion is a biting satire about billionaire smoke and mirrors that sacrifices some whodunit suspense to let Benoit Blanc lay into the moronic upper crust of society.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Johnson could not predict Elon Musk's precise folly in decimating a popular social media app in only a few months. But like Blanc, he's a keen observer of hubris, vanity, and all the traits that make for a toxic personality, yet a beautiful murder mystery
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: The first hour is easily the best part of this sequel.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Rian Johnson takes jabs at excess wealth + toxic influencer culture while keeping the tone facetious and lively. The script fires on all cylinders, delivering a fun whodunit as shrewd as the first movie.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: The central mystery is almost beside the point; instead, the zaniness is the goal. Does it satisfy? Yes, but it’s a little less filling than the first installment.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Johnson certainly delights in creating puzzling distractions, but even if his film is as deep as a layer of onion skin, it is immensely engaging. "Glass Onion" gently mocks its characters, which what makes it so enjoyable
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: Everyone in Rian Johnson’s Glass Onion, the sequel to his unexpectedly delightful 2019 murder mystery Knives Out, seems to be having a blast -- especially the highly accomplished director.
reviews.author: John Wenzel

reviews.text: Glass Onion is not a perfect film... but it makes for a really good time.
reviews.author: Emily Zemler

reviews.text: There’s one dizzying, tantalizing twist after another, and Johnson’s juggling of oodles of narrative threads without cheating is a major accomplishment.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: The complexity and pleasures of Glass Onion lies in its ability to maneuver smoothly between genres. ... Features a powerhouse performance by Janelle Monae.
reviews.author: Peter Martin

reviews.text: Dialogue is witty and there are so many star walk-ons you would have to have a notebook to keep track.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: Nowhere near as good as the first Knives Out, but a decent watch if you are hankering for a mystery and some mindless, wheel-spinning fun.
reviews.author: Alison de Souza

reviews.text: Craig, shed of his dour James Bond stiffness, is enough to carry "Glass Onion" over its rough patches, while Norton and Monáe dine on the meal Johnson puts in front of them.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Both ridiculously opulent and opulently ridiculous, Glass Onion skewers the rich while wallowing in their excesses.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: It’s the filmic equivalent of a Penn and Teller magic trick: amaze, show the mechanics, amaze again.
reviews.author: Jamie Graham

reviews.text: A bright and bubbly whodunit, perfect for holiday-season escapism.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: …Glass Onion offers the same blend of glam, hip comedy and tight, detailed detection that made the first film work so well…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: The film is certainly more over-the-top than the original, yet every bit as entertaining.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Looking every penny of the millions spent on it, Glass Onion understands what audiences responded to with the first film and delivers in the same vein.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is an S-tier modern whodunnit mystery with great direction and excellent performances. One of the most fulfilling film-going experiences I’ve seen this year.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: When too much is cryptic and unfamiliar, viewers will feel stuck outside of the goings-on, which is exactly what happens here, keeping them indifferent and disinterested and dissatisfied.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Glass Onion is an ingenious, self-contained puzzle, which is both funnier and sneakier than its predecessor (and 10 minutes longer)... The script is as tight as the dashing blue cravat knotted around Daniel Craig’s neck.
reviews.author: Damon Smith

reviews.text: While it's not nearly as fun as 2019 predecessor Knives Out, the return of Daniel Craig as private detective Benoit Blanc is enough reason to pop in for another puzzling whodunit.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: Utterly without subtext, completely uninterested in raising anyone’s consciousness about anything, Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is refreshingly focused — in its own, lazy laser sort of way — simply on being fun and frolicsome.
reviews.author: Bill Newcott

reviews.text:
When you see a room full of glass sculpture, you know something is going to break before the visit is up.

And, sure enough, that happens in “Glass Onion – A Knives Out Mystery,” another Rian Johnson treat that smashes more than a glass ceiling.
reviews.author: Bruce R. Miller

reviews.text: Johnson is a master storyteller and knows how to spin a hugely entertaining yarn with a handpicked classy cast. Glass Onion doesn't live up to the cinematic perfection of his first Knives Out but there's plenty of onion goodness here to savour.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: Be prepared to be inscribed with all manner of sublime joys, from actors chewing scenery to witty writing that does loop de loops with its own rococo flourishes. What’s that strange feeling? It’s called fun, damn it!
reviews.author: Dorothy Woodend

reviews.text: Johnson is a canny enough student of the genre to keep Glass Onion from being a letdown, but beyond fleshing out Blanc's personal life and the twist at the midpoint, there's not a ton here to recommend.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Delicious, super fun, and intelligent. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pedro Paunero

reviews.text: Janelle Monáe and Kate Hudson manage to steal scenes while also etching memorable characters. This is easily the funniest comedy of 2022.
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery starts out a little rough, but as each new layer of the mystery gets peeled back like an onion, the film recovers from what appears to be an initial tailspin.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: Rian Johnson has once again elevated the mystery genre with a funnier and even more clever sequel whose takedown of foolishly revered, disruptive billionaires is even more on target now than when it premiered.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: A thoroughly great time!
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: Johnson’s plotting, and the dispensing of information about the characters and the crime, is as intricate and as clever as in “Knives Out.” What’s different is an added layer of comedy, mostly provided by the continued exploration of Blanc.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: So finely and delicately chopped and browned. Sharper than Knives.
reviews.author: Caffeinated Clint

reviews.text: Glass Onion is another rollicking mystery that continues the Knives Out series wonderfully - even if it isn’t quite as beguiling as its predecessor.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: The ensemble cast is fabulous, and Johnson’s script is clever.
reviews.author: Collin Garbarino

reviews.text: Rian Johnson has pulled off the impossible. He’s followed up his wildly successful Knives Out with a second instalment that is just as fun, just as clever and just as brilliant as the first.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: It is deadly fun and games at the expense of the new American elite. It is 86ing the 1%, and it is 100 times more entertaining that you could imagine.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: A fast-moving satirical spoof that bristles with clever ideas, giving the beautiful people and uber successful a serve if not as many laughs as the original
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: 140 minutes simply uses an exciting story, lots of ingenuity, and likable characters roughly.  [Full review in Spanish[]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: It makes for a profoundly empty viewing experience.
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text:
GlassOnion is a brilliantly written sequel with strong performances and hilarious moments.

Rian Johnson ‘s passion for the murder mystery genre is evident throughout and Daniel Craig is clearly having the time of his life as Benoit Blanc.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: Johnson's plotting is impeccable, creating mystery after mystery with clever deceptions, clues dropped so quickly you won't see them, and ultimately satisfying denouncements.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Everyone's doing stellar work in Glass Onion, especially the killer cast.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Norton and Hudson are the standouts in the cast of frenemies, both demonstrating very sharp comic timing.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: I feel like they had a good time filming this, and a lot of times that translates into how you enjoy a movie.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: Rian Johnson shows irresistible skill with this sprightly, elegant and occasionally ingenious concoction.
reviews.author: Michael Medved

reviews.text: It’s one of the best comedies of the year masquerading as one of the best mysteries of the year, with knife-sharp dialogue, heightened performances, and an interlocking series of twisty puzzles at its center.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: “Glass Onion” will easily charm even the most demanding viewers.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: At several points in the film, Craig’s Benoit Blanc is referred to as “the world’s greatest detective.” Glass Onion, in turn, is one of the world’s greatest detective movies.
reviews.author: Matt Baume

reviews.text: By the end, it becomes crystal clear that Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is an event movie.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: Rian Johnson has done it again. Just like an Agatha Christie novel, Glass Onion feels fresh and even bigger than the previous Knives Out mystery. It scratches that same whodunnit itch as the first, but it also feels entirely different.
reviews.author: Sara Clements

reviews.text: A timely, winding murder mystery with a glimmer of mischief in its eye, [Glass Onion] is as just as slick as its predecessor, but it has no interest in re-treading familiar ground.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: The movie's fun, it's funny, sometimes it's funny to its detriment, but I overall enjoyed myself.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: There's no sophomore slump here.
reviews.author: Sarah Rappaport

reviews.text: There’s nothing like confidence to buoy a film into reaching for greatness, and Johnson has confidence in spades here.
reviews.author: Owen Gabbey

reviews.text: Very likable. My audience applauded at the end. Most audiences will, I suspect. There are many adults who will watch this more than once on Netflix next month.
reviews.author: David Poland

reviews.text: It’s just a few inches behind Knives Out. But that’s complaining about a dish you don’t like on a magnificent tasting menu. It’s not as good as the best tasting menu, but just enjoy the great movie, dude.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: It's so glossy, over-produced, and swank... I didn't find the cast all that sterling.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: We should have several movies a month like this. I'm glad Rian Johnson is the person who keeps making them.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Bautista, Hudson and Monáe are the standouts, but really everyone gets a chance to shine so its hard to single out. Everyone is just that good.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: For all its barbed points, Glass Onion is one long guilt-free holiday in the sun. With double Knives Out’s budget, it has all the lavish pleasures and communal affect you’d want at the cinema.
reviews.author: Nick Hasted

reviews.text: Johnson's screenplay is consistently fleet-footed and funny, deftly peeling back the layers of the story and having a blast doing it.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: While it might not have quite the richly satisfying subtext of the original, that sense of nearly perfect coherency, there is still a tremendous amount of fun to be had.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Rian Johnson, who’s evidently incapable of directing a movie that isn’t fun, brings you the season’s most fun film.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: A delightful trifle of a mystery movie, a laugh-out-loud comedy that deserves to be a mass market theatrical hit.
reviews.author: Ani Bundel

reviews.text: Each archetype fits its puzzle piece impeccably and elevates the themes. This close examination of current culture is a difficult task. Yet, Rian Johnson does so ingeniously.
reviews.author: Andres Cabrera

reviews.text: I dare you not to laugh-out-loud, at Daniel Craig's outrageous accusations--who knew James Bond could be so comical?
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives out Mystery is the perfect blend of writing, direction, and production while not forgetting the cardinal rules of a great mystery.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Rian Johnson proves once again that he is a brilliant writer, especially with the humor, as Glass Onion is even funnier than its predecessor.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Glass Onion wisely avoids trying to top its predecessor’s sentimentality. Rather, the film pushes deeper into playfulness, while still maintaining a poignant streak.
reviews.author: Shirley Li

reviews.text: The actors evidently consider this type of movie to be a frolic, and their sense of fun is contagious.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Glass Onion establishes Benoit Blanc as this generation's detective icon. The clever and witty writing paired with an electric cast serves a mystery that is just as good (if not better) than Knives Out. This franchise is destined to be timelessly classic.
reviews.author: Cody Leach

reviews.text: Knives Out may have bottled a cultural moment, but Glass Onion seems built for longevity: it’s populist entertainment with its head screwed on right. And there’s plenty of value in that.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Glass Onion is a brighter, louder, more extroverted movie than the first Knives Out.
reviews.author: Oli Welsh

reviews.text: Simple and even vulgar intrigue mixed with the tiresome riddle of the murderer's identity transforms before the eyes of the surprised audience into a motley display of talent as funny as it is sagacious and labyrinthine. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: How much you'll enjoy "Glass Onion" may depend entirely on your fondness for ridiculous coincidence and crowded contrivance , but none of it is meant to be taken seriously.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Johnson is clearly more tickled by the Who than the Dunnit. Once it arrives, the actual murder case is treated like a chore.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Johnson meticulously crafts a simple yet layered new mystery that becomes about the experience of watching the ensemble go nuts.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: As it turns out, the answers fill a cornucopia with oxymorons. "Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery" is awfully good at making its small crowd of pretty ugly people and terrific liars stand out amid open secrets and loyal opposition.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: I liked Glass Onion a little more than Knives Out. It's really great fun and I enjoyed the performances and a lot of the characters and the twists and turns.
reviews.author: Eric Goldman

reviews.text: Glass Onion improves on the original, taking a character we know and love and thrusting him into a funnier and more zany mystery.
reviews.author: Christopher James

reviews.text: The biggest shock of the new Knives Out is how contemporary it feels.  Director Rian Johnson isn’t playing some old game of Clue.  He wants to talk about our world.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: Rian Johnson has created another exceptional murder mystery playing with characters we know all too well in our current culture.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: The ingenuity here lies in the story construct. “Glass Onion: Knives Out Mystery” takes translucent jabs at political, social, economic and entertainment elites in a polarized society, while delivering a masterful mystery and whodunit entertainment.
reviews.author: Nathalia Aryani

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is as layered as its name suggests, with enjoyable performances, witty dialog, and biting humor.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: The script is smart, scathing in its humor at times, and we get a full understanding of our characters – not an easy thing to do while also threading a murder mystery through the arcs.
reviews.author: Jean Henegan

reviews.text: [Director Rian] Johnson pushes the envelope on how much raucous fun one can have while trying to solve a murder ... The ride, like the peeling of an onion, will leave you crying for more.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Fans of Knives Out will surely enjoy the result, albeit with the slightly diminished enthusiasm that’s customary for a sequel.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: A delightfully fiendish romp filled with snarky characters, loads of visual humor, and a loosey-goosey Daniel Craig...Janelle Monaé is so good it would be a crime for her not to be nominated for Best Supporting Actress.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: What really killed me is that I hardly laughed at all.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: A danged blast. It's bracing, zingy, whipsmart not afraid to poke fun at the pandemic, mock a somehow familiar, attention-seeking, infantile tech mogul, to skewer social media and generally rebel against the now.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: There are few franchises where the followup exceeds the original, but director Rian Johnson  seems to be getting better with franchise age. The multilayered Glass Onion is more fabulous and even more fun than its predecessor.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Good fun, if at times leaving you with the unhelpful suspicion that writer-director Rian Johnson and his cast might be having 25 per cent more of a hoot than their audience.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Rian Johnson again proves his ability to subvert a genre while elevating it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: Stretches its premise so thin that the cleverness never feels all that satisfying.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Rian Johnson is no stranger to crafting sequels that far outshine the first film in a trilogy, but this time he’s proving that he can eclipse even his own brilliant storytelling with fresh twists and a new cast of characters worthy of despising.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: Looser, flabbier but fun.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: Craig’s Blanc [is] simply one of the most compelling and charismatic creations of modern cinema.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Daniel Craig and Janelle Monáe lead perfect casting which benefits a complex script that, while not QUITE to the same level of its predecessor, is nonetheless remarkable on its own merit for building on its established formula.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: It’s a massive amount of fun, too elegant and self-aware to even consider criticising, and Craig brings more depth to the conceited but lovable sleuth. More of this please.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: Maybe the novelty of Benoit Blanc has worn off, but Glass Onion still holds the delights of a well-plotted puzzle plot and more incidental pleasures.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: In Glass Onion, everything is more. More jokes. More self-reflexivity. More twists and turns. And, undeniably, more fun.
reviews.author: Kathy Michelle Chacón

reviews.text: It’s just not as sharp as its predecessor, though the cameos by Hugh Grant, Ethan Hawke and Serena Williams are spikes of punchy good fun.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Glass Onion is a late year present from a director who rarely disappoints.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Jackie Hoffman, as Bautista's mother, gets to utter, possibly for the first time ever in a semi-genteel, English-style murder mystery, the words "Fibonacci sequence."
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: As a sequel that improves on the original, Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery, is a rarity.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: … engages on so many levels that it dazzles.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: The pleasure of Glass Onion (besides the delicious cast) comes from discovering halfway through that you're watching an entirely different film than you originally thought, as it was with Knives Out as well.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: The production takes advantage of the warm and sunny locale and beautiful people as the backdrop for a clever little mystery. It does not mean I will go back and watch the first again, but maybe I will greet future entries more kindly.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Even though it is absurd, mystery fans should find “Glass Onion” to be good decadent fun.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is not only better than the original but it is the best movie of 2022.
reviews.author: Thomas White

reviews.text: Glass Onion is certainly on a par with its predecessor ... it is that dazzling, riveting ensemble piece that we have been waiting for ... Daniel Craig is truly in his element reprising his role as Blanc
reviews.author: Latoya Austin

reviews.text: One film was already enough to satisfy, but plenty of evidence presented shows that Rian Johnson knows how to assemble more than one kind of mystery.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Glass Onion is a marvel to watch, at once gleeful and diverting while not lacking thematic resonance. It elicits a sense of wonder as Johnson pulls off a feat of engineering, creating pure pleasure with a finale that delivers satisfaction...
reviews.author: Kimber Myers

reviews.text: It’s whip-smart, joyful, and more than a little bit mischievous, yet another manipulation/reinvention of the classic whodunit, made with a cast whose thrill to be working produces an experience that’s as exuberant for them as it is for viewers.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: Less of a Thanksgiving treat than its predecessor....As a puzzle “Onion” passes muster, but while one can admire the ingeniousness of the clockwork mechanism Johnson sets running here, as it counts down it proves to be less fun than it should.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Daniel Craig probes a new mystery in the clever but not-as-fun-as-the-first 'Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery.'
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: Blanc feels one draft, one rewrite away from a truly distinctive creation. Easier said than done; meantime, Craig’s filling in the blancs very nicely indeed.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: As he did in “Knives Out,” Johnson craftily weaves in a strong plot thread of the haves versus the have-nots. That inclusion feels less clunky this time; the outcome is equally enjoyable in its schadenfreude.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: Johnson is also a master of misdirection, toying with us just enough so that we’re not sure when we’re being given a clue versus when we’re being handed a playful red herring.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: When pop cinema is powered by ruthless intelligence, it’s good for everyone.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: The film is spectacular to look at, so try to catch this in theaters when you can. And it’s one of those rare treats that is actually more fun to watch a second and third time (which I have done, so you can trust me).
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: I haven't had this much fun at the movies in a long time.
reviews.author: Tania Lamb

reviews.text: A very well packaged, light-hearted jaunt, peppered with satirical jabs at online culture, influencers and “disrupters” and featuring lovely, cheesy performances from a top ensemble. But as fun as the film is, should you see a Netflix film at the cinema?
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Writer/director Rian Johnson disrupts his own formula in clever, mysterious ways.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: “Glass Onion” doesn’t build to a sharp finale, it plays more like a television variety show.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: While different in tone and structure from the previous film, this one is even more rapturously entertaining than its predecessor. It is also quite a bit funnier.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: To quote Gertrude Stein, "there's no there there."  And after two hours plus, I was weary of watching the spinning ball.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: A sequel that's better than the original movie. Glass Onion admirably avoids one of the biggest mistakes that most movie sequels make: It doesn't try to copy its predecessor. To put it in baseball terms: It swings big in its ambitions and hits a home run.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: [An] uproarious if slightly inferior sequel.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Boasts a brilliant engaging screenplay that may not be as sharp as its predecessor, but does have enough layers to appreciate; the twists mingled among the well-timed editing & led by Daniel Craig’s charisma make Glass Onion a sequel worth watching.
reviews.author: Jason Escamilla

reviews.text: Johnson, who once again also penned the script, has no shortage of ammunition for his rat-a-tat takes on pop-culture ephemera and the navel-gazing delusions of wealth and fame.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: In this kind of film, once you know the identity of the murderer the tension goes out the window. But Rian Johnson is sure to avoid this with a spectacular climax that makes this film more fun and agile than its predecessor. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Silly, clever, and totally riveting whodunnit that rewards close attention and demands an immediate rewatch. Peel slowly and see.
reviews.author: Amelia Berry

reviews.text: There’s a good deal of fun in Glass Onion... [But] the movie has a slight case of the diminishing-return blues.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: This satirical whodunit peels back the layers of modern-day movers and shakers to reveal that, when you get to the core of an arrogant genius, a fabulous fashionista, or a blowhard YouTuber, there's often nothing there.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Writer-director Rian Johnson again assembles a solid cast behind Daniel Craig, but it’s his use of language -- where nary a word is wasted -- that finally gives the sequel its edge.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: Glass Onion is the most fun I've had at the movies in 2022, and I beg you to see it in theaters with an audience.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Deliciously hilarious in peeling this millennia's rich and famous: new tech magnates, models, youtubers, influencers, and an etcetera who will gather just as Agatha Christie's cannon dictates... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text: An exhilarating enjoyment of twists, puzzles and meta cinema. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Janire Zurbano

reviews.text: The joy of Glass Onion is that you can read into it, or just let it flow over you and enjoy the ride.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: It’s bigger, wilder and funnier than its predecessor.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: Glass Onion still has the edge over the year’s other whodunnits, if only because of the sublime Monáe.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: Johnson’s fiendishly entertaining concoction rarely disappoints thanks to his dazzling dispersal of clues, red-herrings, narrative trickery, sly cameos and wry performances.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Glass Onion is ridiculously clever, a moveable puzzle box that skewers the super-wealthy and the company they keep
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: Keeps up some of the mad-cappery and sleight-of-hand plotting of the original, while still succeeding in feeling fresh and novel.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: It’s an all-new mystery with new players, and while the wicked guessing-game concept of the original is intact, the particulars are very different.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Another momentarily entertaining sequel, that suffers from unrestrained excess.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: It’s a bigger, showier follow-up, from the A-list cast to the twistier twists, even if it doesn’t have the same witty punch as the original.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: "Glass Onion" is more than just a sequel to "Knives Out." It is a director confidently making the movies that he wants to in a manner that only he can.
reviews.author: Derek Deskins

reviews.text: Glass Onion is a fun time that begs to be experienced with others.
reviews.author: Thomas Stoneham-Judge

reviews.text: The first one was good … this one is better: an ingenious, headspinningly preposterous and enjoyable new whodunnit romp featuring Daniel Craig as the legendary detective from the deep south, Benoit Blanc.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: This is a whip-smart, consistently funny and sure to be crowd-pleasing affair.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Let’s give thanks for this wicked, whacked-out whodunit sequel.. Daniel Craig is back as southern-fried detective Benoit Blanc and all is right with this crazy world as a cast of merry pranksters (yay Janelle Monae) turns murder most foul into comic gold.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: For all that self-aware fuss, Glass Onion works darn well as a mystery romp. It is a little smooth to the touch, but there are beautiful chicanes along the route to a satisfactorily clamorous conclusion.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: A sizzling spectacular of a whodunit with a labyrinth of twists that makes you lean in to decipher not who or why but how messed up these people are, and all the clues were there all along.
reviews.author: Sherin Nicole

reviews.text: Johnson and the actors make the playful, barbed interactions between the characters a delight, all while seeding clues for the eventual solution to the crime.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: More than a mere whodunnit, it’s a satire on society that leads us carefully by the hand to a stunning dénouement designed to jolt us like a thunderbolt. And it does.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Glass Onion is as much a creative success as its predecessor.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The fact that Johnson was able to follow up his crackerjack whodunnit with another that is equally fantastic is a testament to a filmmaker working at the height of his powers.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: The puzzle-box production design by Rick Heinrichs is an absolute delight.
reviews.author: Randall King

reviews.text: Glass Onion is so good that you can easily see Johnson returning every few years with a fresh cast. Other than Blanc, Johnson is not relying on the same tricks this time around, indicating his creativity knows no bounds.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: Leave it to screenwriter/director Rian Johnson to give us the perfect holiday after-dinner aperitif, a sparkler worth imbibing more than once with family and friends.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: The enormously appealing thing about “Glass Onion” is watching the cast have an obviously good time with their characters and with each other.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: More fun and more comedic than its predecessor. The twists resonate stronger than the original and are not as easy to see coming. Plus, the reveals (of which there are a few) resonate with the satisfaction of a game well played.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: Norton emits a hilariously potent eau de Elon Musk...
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Glass Onion gets off to a rocky start, but the film takes off once our hilarious group of characters come together and clash with one another. This mystery is a fun one, and Daniel Craig is in top form.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: "Knives Out" remains a fantastic film on successive rewatches and Johnson’s follow-up tale, "Glass Onion," follows in that vein, taking conventions and twisting them all around so that we aren’t sure what to believe and we’re delighted all the same.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: One of the purest pop pleasures of the season, the kind of irresistible crowd-pleaser that balances its franchise obligations with a clear sense of wit and creative purpose.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Whether they see it on a big screen or small, viewers will no doubt instantly recognize the new batch of characters invented by writer-director Rian Johnson, whose timing and satirical targets have once again proved utterly uncanny.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: A fizzy, gaudy, joyfully entertaining couple of hours. If there’s any right in the world, Rian Johnson and Daniel Craig will continue making films in the Benoit Blanc Cinematic Universe forever.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: A breezy caper that mostly sustains its novelty, even if it stumbles a bit in the last third.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Prescient is Norton’s engulf-and-devour Elon Musk-like prick billionaire, an asset-grabber given to malapropisms in a role that fits him like a pair of skinny trousers.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: A bigger, gaudier, twistier affair than its predecessor. (The hideous, naked greed evinced by the suspects remains the same, of course.)
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: I can’t say much about what happens in “Glass Onion” without giving away some surprises, but I can say that some of the pleasure comes from being wrong about what will happen next.
reviews.author: A.O. Scott

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is a wildly good time with consistent laughs and dazzling production value.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Daniel Craig is just through-the-roof entertaining as Blanc; his Foghorn Leghorn accent is even more welcome the second time around.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: Beginning with the fact that the great Kathryn Hahn is wasted in an underwritten role and concluding with a climax which could have been entirely foregone with a simple device introduced earlier, “Glass Onion” is an empty calorie snack.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: 'Glass Onion' carries over a portion of its predecessor’s pumped-up energy, but the narrative blades have admittedly lost some of their sharpness and shine. The smart writing we expected doesn’t sustain due to the sequel's goofy, less compelling mystery.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Rowdier, richer, and sometimes a little more ungainly than its predecessor, Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is more evidence that Rian Johnson is the most democratic director since Jonathan Demme.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: You watch “Glass Onion” relaxed, feeling like you’re in good hands; everyone on-screen is clearly having a wonderful time, so you can’t help but join right in.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Glass Onion has more twists than Chubby Checker’s discography.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: Funnier and more manic than the first film, even if there’s an irony in seeking to satirize the immodesty of tech-bubble billionaires by setting as much of Netflix’s money on fire as humanly possible,
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: A sharper and more complete whodunit than the first.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: As entertaining as the first Benoit Blanc mystery was, I think this one is slightly better.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: It’s a movie every bit as fun as its predecessor, with just as much to say, and it’s easily one of the most satisfying times you’ll have with a movie this year.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: To Johnson, satire, commentary aside, can and should amuse as much as it elucidates and there’s certainly no shortage of both.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: Glass Onion isn’t breaking new ground, but it isn’t trying to, either. A fun caper with just enough bite to give it some meaning, it’s the kind of entertainment that is easy to recommend.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: Craig settles into his post-Bond role with smooth, comedic ease, flexing hammy chops of loquacious, Southern-fried, cigar-smoking hokum that were never part of his arsenal as OO7.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: Johnson’s twist-packed script and sight-gag-packed frame offer something few contemporary blockbusters do: attunement to the audience’s emotional response in the moment.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: The bottom line is that Johnson has established a tone, a style and a lead character that should serve him well for years.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Despite Glass Onion not being as smart as Knives Out, it was definitely just as entertaining—if not more.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: One of the most entertaining and pleasing films of the year. Rian Johnson's newest whodunit entry delivers in every filmmaking department. It's funny, ambitious, timely and so much fun. Somehow even better than the original. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: The laughs come quickly and regularly, stemming from smart satire, wild dialogue, and a quippy edit that finds many punchlines through simple filmic construction.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: The real star? Johnson’s crisply mischievous screenplay, which crams in so many laughs you almost don’t notice the occasional plot holes.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Perfection isn’t objective, it’s subjective and Glass Onion provides everything I need and want from a film like this; surprises, laughs and a central mystery full of suspense.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: The only gripe one could have against it would be Johnson’s decision to move the film from classic whodunnit to something altogether sillier and more out there.
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: It is shiny with mischief, crafted with guile, and performed with eager wit... Why, then, should the whole enterprise feel so curiously thin and cold to the touch?
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: The brilliant writing, editing, and direction come together along with the stellar cast performances in order to keep viewers entertained from start to finish.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Clever and funny, this traditional murder mystery is quite an enjoyable ride.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is a bigger and more bombastic film than its predecessor -- and lives up to the first film's prestige.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: Still worthwhile, one should be prepared for Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery to not live up to the expectations and refreshing identity of the first film.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: “Glass Onion” is a romp with a sly sense of humor and plenty of clever cameos thrown in to spice things up.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: Glass Onion is so cleverly and distressingly prescient. Some of its timeliness is serendipity; the larger share is a smart writer and director who understands that the roots of these sad farces are as old as our country.
reviews.author: Adam Kempenaar

reviews.text: The most notable performance is that of Janelle Monae, who proves she is every bit as accomplished at acting as she is singing.
reviews.author: Grant Rollings

reviews.text: Fantastic film, even better than the first one! Biting, clever, timely commentary that's also hilarious, plus a genuine mystery. With a proof of concept, Johnson & Craig are both bolder this time and the Knives Out franchise is better for it.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Johnson sits midway between Wes Anderson and Christopher Nolan, while being much breezier and more likeable than either. Glass Onion is as irresistibly entertaining as all his work, though not lacking in layers of ambiguity if you look for them.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: While it lacks the sleekness of the original, Glass Onion does something rare for anticipated sequels: it actually finds a way to work.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: “Glass Onion” stands well on its own as a deliciously satisfying romp, driven by Johnson’s signature snarky wit and knack for savory dialogue.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: An electric standalone sequel by writer/director Rian Johnson with nearly all of the same bugs and features of his predecessor, albeit with new flavoring.
reviews.author: Eric Francisco

reviews.text: Rian Johnson delivers another rousing injection of immersive thrills with another eclectic livewire ensemble, although the story has one too many layers
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Not shaken at the word sequel, but certainly stirring up the whodunnit genre, Glass Onion takes another stab at the murder mystery, triumphs at sleuthing audiences once again. But the vulgarity alone almost killed the entertainment.
reviews.author: Christie Cronan

reviews.text: While Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery offers a lot of the same scrumptious twists and class warfare satire as the first film, Johnson takes the zaniness up so high it very nearly toppled the whole affair.
reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

reviews.text: For the amount of entertainment Rian Johnson has given me, I may owe him my first born. If so, I’ll name the baby Glass Onion Knives Out. Or vice versa, whichever works for you.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: Fun. Remember fun? Rian Johnson knows we could use a good dose of it and serves us up a gleefully good time.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: A perfect blend of actors who put their own stamp on their characters. Rian Johnson gives us a worthy follow-up to the 2019 original.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Felt like I was watching a bunch of famous people take a vacation in Greece and that’s not my idea of a good time. No thanks.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Rian Johnson surprises with an investigation that's way funnier than its predecessor without sacrificing the credibility of the story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: "Glass Onion" is a dazzling and delightful whodunit!
reviews.author: Leah Sydney

reviews.text: Like the first film, Glass Onion is an engine of entertainment, and as an engine, hearing this baby purr under the hood is sweet music all its own.
reviews.author: Alan Cerny

reviews.text: This second stab is another twist-filled treat, having fun with the whodunnit genre while also just being very funny.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: This smart, sassy murder-mystery establishes Daniel Craig’s Benoit Blanc as a Poirot for the super-rich era.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: The mystery whodunit breaks no new ground but is highly entertaining.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Glass Onion is best experienced with as little prior knowledge as possible, as the surprises that lie beneath every peeled layer shock and delight in equal measure
reviews.author: Rhys Bowen Jones

reviews.text: It’s bold and pays off; even if you think you know who’s behind it all, the crafty way information is doled out ensures you would never know how or why.
reviews.author: Trace Sauveur

reviews.text: With its exquisite style and deconstruction of the influencer culture, Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery is a dazzling murder mystery ripe with laughs, twists, and performances to die for.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: The sequel is lighter and funnier than the original, which occasionally felt a bit heavy-handed while pitting the haves vs. the have-nots.
reviews.author: Tricia Gilbride

reviews.text: In proving that the first film was no fluke and the depth of his talents, Rian Johnson delivers another passionate love letter to the murder mystery genre.
reviews.author: Kelechi Ehenulo

reviews.text: [T]he real triumph of the film is watching the eclectic cast as they bounce off of each other while delivering Johnson’s often-hilarious dialogue.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Look, it's all a bit of innocuous fun, and would land without quibble if the story was as strong as Knives Out.
reviews.author: Lucy Ford

reviews.text: While Knives Out sets the tone for the modern murder mystery, Glass Onion picks it up and continues it with aplomb...Johnson’s words and the buoyant performances raise the bar on this sequel.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Think of all those movies made during the Depression... “Glass Onion” contains the same class-conscious escapism, dastardly behavior, clever twists and genuine surprise, while being totally modern and laugh-out-loud fun. Movies are fun again!
reviews.author: Sarah Manvel

reviews.text: In a cast of standouts, Janelle Monáe rises above all of them.
reviews.author: Karen M. Peterson

reviews.text: This is yet another stellar example of the murder mystery genre that expands on the views of its predecessor, whilst also delving deeper into Blanc’s mentality and creating a compelling cast of new characters to boot.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: A serious case of sequelitis — it’s bigger, louder, emptier.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Like its precursor, Glass Onion doubles as a dazzlingly engineered gizmo and a raucous cautionary satire, with implications that billow out into the world even as its mechanisms snap satisfyingly shut.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Glass Onion, Rian Johnson’s uproarious, dazzling Netflix sequel to Knives Out, is a triumph and tragedy; no movie this good should be confined to the cell of a streaming platform.
reviews.author: Cameron Frew

reviews.text: Knives Out put the fun back into film whodunits, and Glass Onion ramps that up. Deliciously scripted by Johnson, it is a spry comic look at how the other half live.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: If you like your gaudy whodunits stirred but not shaken, this might be for you.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: With a clever script, characters that perfectly satire the modern ruling class, and the crowd-pleasing antics that won over "Knives Out" audiences, "Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery" is a pure delight.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: This long-awaited adventure delivers layer upon layer of wit, fun and mystery, thanks to its phenomenal and hilarious cast. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: With a compelling leading lady in Janelle Monáe and an ensemble cast filled to the brim with comedic talent, Glass Onion is a rollicking good time and a clever mystery that more than does justice to the Knives Out name.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: Johnson turns the volume up to eleven with his follow-up, Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery, and manages to deliver one fine rollercoaster of a film that is every bit as entertaining and refreshing as its predecessor.
reviews.author: Emma Badame

reviews.text: If Knives Out was about the moral dry rot of old money and classism, Glass Onion is about the moral decay of new money and influencers.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: With Glass Onion, Johnson takes us on a brand-new adventure, one bathed in the same magical style of the first film and with a notable through-line in its satirical commentary on the rich and powerful.
reviews.author: Ileana Meléndez

reviews.text: Glass Onion is just a great time watching a movie. It’s a rare movie (especially at a film festival where I have places I have to be) in which I wished it were longer.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: The appeal of Craig’s magnanimously verbose super-sleuth is real, as is Johnson’s ability to craft—and execute—a multilayered suspense plot whose solution is, as per the Beatles-derived structure of the title, visible in plain sight.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Another masterful murder mystery from Rian Johnson. Just like the first film, Glass Onion will warrant multiple viewings to fully soak in the wild amount of precision and passion that went into the film.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Just like peeling an onion, Johnson masterfully reveals his rich set of characters while keeping us surprised throughout with twists that keep coming.
reviews.author: Mina Takla

reviews.text: Glass Onion is good escapism without aspiring to surpass the genre’s masters, and that worked for me for this iteration.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: So who did it? Why, the actors, of course. They're largely responsible for delivering the generally snappy goods.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Glass Onion excels, particularly in the middle half of the film, at creating a satisfying narrative. But the large-scale ending overtook the feeling of satisfaction provided by its predecessor.
reviews.author: Hannah Lodge

reviews.text: This delightful sequel is proof that while the magic of watching your favorite film for the first time is gone, the chance to relive it is still very much alive through equally great retellings.
reviews.author: Alicia Gilstorf

reviews.text: Gets off to a bit of a slow start, but something clicks about halfway through and it’s nothing but glorious payoffs until the end.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Only Daniel Craig is back from the first film but the film does not suffer any. Actually, it is better as it keeps things fresh.
reviews.author: Carey-Ann Pawsey

reviews.text: Rian Johnson provides a pitch perfect follow up to his predecessor with more barbs, quips and whiplash twists and turns from a cast led by Janelle Monae and Daniel Craig
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: As a whole mid-tier of movies has eroded from our screens, it becomes a relief to at least see something confident in the pleasure of watching people on screen.
reviews.author: Jesse Nussman

reviews.text: Movies like Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery are the reason to do any sequel in the first place
reviews.author: Amber Dowling

reviews.text: Rian Johnson succeeds in making Glass Onion a worthy follow up to Knives Out and delivers an entertaining, character driven, funny and captivating mystery.
reviews.author: Ricky Church

reviews.text: An equally enjoyable, bitingly sharp, and beautifully crafted murder mystery from Rian Johnson.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Johnson keeps things light over a fleet 130 minutes and sticks the landing.
reviews.author: Vadim Rizov

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery improves upon virtually every aspect of its predecessor and delivers a big, bold, funny, angry, timely, and timeless whodunit.
reviews.author: Rafael Motamayor

reviews.text: Johnson has presented a puzzle box sequel, Glass Onion, that's phenomenal, fun, gorgeous, and absolutely thrilling.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: The root of the issues with Glass Onion can be found within its central metaphor -- as many say in the film, it’s got lots of layers, but it’s still transparent and empty at the core -- because the film’s script is just a nightmare.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: As a film about the intricate joys of puzzle-solving, it’s plain to see Johnson getting his kicks in the same way, reveling in complexity and bringing us with him as he untangles it.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: Craig arguably delivers some of his best work in this film, but Monáe completely steals the show.
reviews.author: Alysha Prasad

reviews.text: Rian Johnson’s follow-up to 2019’s Knives Out is a wholly superior whodunit contraption, at once more complex, cunning, and laugh-out-loud amusing.
reviews.author: Nick Schager
