reviews.text: The first Knives Out remains a delight that repays return visits; Glass Onion is a very funny one-and-done.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Rian Johnson’s latest stab at Wes Anderson-does-Clue has a lesser cast, a more pandering script, and a wholly phony “Eat the Rich” political angle.
reviews.author: Sam C. Mac

reviews.text: Glass Onion is not only a worthy successor to the 2019 megahit, but it’s glossy, sexy, and hilarious. You won’t have a better time at the movies.
reviews.author: Joey Moser

reviews.text: Glass Onion is a layered machine hiding a trove of interlocking rewards, immensely satisfying when the pieces reveal themselves, but even more so when it’s all blown to bits.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: Making a film this entertaining and broadly appearing isn’t an easy task, let alone for a sequel to match its predecessor’s reputation, but Johnson flexes the notion of having his cake and eating it too with inherent ease.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Glass Onion may not have the charm of the first movie, but it's enough to keep fans watching for future instalments.
reviews.author: Alex Hudson

reviews.text: It might be foolhardy to claim that Johnson has produced a socially conscious murder mystery, and yet there’s a sobering motif within the plot: namely, the moral compromises that proximity to great wealth tempts people with.
reviews.author: Nicolas Rapold

reviews.text: Once again, over two hours and 19 minutes, writer-director Rian Johnson weaves an intricate, complicated tapestry. And once again, he ties up every last loose end with a satisfying flourish.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: The climax has a certain primally cathartic power, but it doesn’t quite dispel the air of self-satisfaction that envelops the script.
reviews.author: Kenji Fujishima

reviews.text: Rian Johnson has even more twisty fun in store for you with Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: ... A one-location whodunnit that feels less Agatha Christie and more The Long Goodbye. At least, this is how it feels when its comedy is working, its twists are twisting, and its satire is the good kind of heavy-handed.
reviews.author: Drew Gregory

reviews.text: Glass Onion is a beautiful-to-look-at feature that is a total gas. There’s a lot of fun to be had while watching gorgeously costumed, loveable actors flutter through a stunning manor, spitting out lines that allow us to laugh at their expense.
reviews.author: Lindsay Traves

reviews.text: ... The cast is more eclectic, the mystery is more complex, and rich assholes are richer and more asshole-y. In short, the sequel is a delight.
reviews.author: Andrew Webster

reviews.text: It will probably take no time at all for spoilers to start arriving online, but Johnson is ahead of that too. Glass Onion will be just as much fun to watch a second time, knowing even more than Blanc does.
reviews.author: Caryn James

reviews.text: Craig has succeeded in creating and expanding a now-iconic screen character in Benoit Blanc, and one that is worthy of his own franchise.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Fear not: Glass Onion is a zippy ride just like Knives Out. I just hope that in his third outing, Detective Blanc finds himself in a humble old regular-sized mansion. That’s where he works best.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: Combined with a fabulous ensemble cast, this whodunit follow-up to Knives Out (which takes a dig at the beloved Clue game) is deeply enjoyable.
reviews.author: Mae Abdulbaki

reviews.text: It’s very hard to make a film this thoroughly satisfying and broadly appealing, and it’s hard to make a sequel that lives up to the standard set by the first. Rian Johnson just did both and made it look easy.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: As popcorn entertainment, Glass Onion	is effective and breathes additional life into the nascent Knives Out franchise, but as a murder mystery, the film is largely a vegetable.
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: The more expansive story makes this sequel feel less tightly wound or exhilarating than its predecessor. But it goes harder on bringing the entertainment and maintaining the magic of Benoit Blanc’s sleuthing expertise.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery avoids sequel troubles because this film is an absolute blast.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: A lot has happened since 2019, and “Glass Onion” acknowledges the Covid-19 pandemic in its opening sequences. But it hasn’t anticipated genre-shifting game-changers like “Bodies Bodies Bodies” and “Triangle of Sadness” now driving the conversation.
reviews.author: Martin Tsai

reviews.text: Glass Onion is bigger and more precisely designed than Knives Out, but what makes it a more satisfying movie is that it sits with its characters more rather than immediately showing off their decay.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Murder. Mayhem. Mediocrity.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: Subtly echoes and departs from its predecessor, maintaining the usual high quality standards without lapsing too blithely into formula.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: How do you give audiences more of what they liked while still surprising them? Glass Onion is the answer.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: A film that delights in explaining to its audience all that they have missed, and somehow eliciting smiles rather than sneers.
reviews.author: Christopher Schobert

reviews.text: Wildly entertaining, and boasts one of the best casts and scripts of the year. Will be endlessly rewatchable when it hits Netflix.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: It's all just so much fun. There’s a contagious aspect to the ensemble in that one can easily tell that they just had a blast making this movie on a Greek isle with dialogue as incredibly smart as Johnson's.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: A glorious, beautiful puzzle box that's a shwer cinematic delight. Beautifully written and structured, its anchored by performances that ooze fun and wit. Takes no sleuthing to know this one of the most fun film experiences of the year
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: It’s so much fun to watch Johnson in this mode, especially with a cast this relentlessly fun and playful. With Glass Onion, Johnson proves himself to be a film disruptor of the highest order.
reviews.author: Ross Bonaime

reviews.text: This picture offers more action, more delicious comeuppances, more daring design and a few genuinely surprising cameos just for good measure.
reviews.author: John DeFore

reviews.text: It’s hard not to have fun when Johnson pulls the strings, I just wish he’d not pulled quite so many and quite so hard.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: “Glass Out” expands into something even more extravagant than the first “Knives Out,” which is what you want, even if at moments it can feel like a little more than you want.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: If you loved Benoit Blanc in “Knives Out”... seeing him tossed into the deep end of yet another wacky-rich whodunit will only further bewitch you.
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: Rian Johnson outdoes himself with Glass Onion.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: In “Glass Onion,” the filmmaker shows absolute mastery of his genre and his craft. It’s pure pop pleasure.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

synopsis: Benoit Blanc returns to peel back the layers in a new Rian Johnson whodunit. This fresh adventure finds the intrepid detective at a lavish private estate on a Greek island, but how and why he comes to be there is only the first of many puzzles. Blanc soon meets a distinctly disparate group of friends gathering at the invitation of billionaire Miles Bron for their yearly reunion. Among those on the guest list are Miles' former business partner Andi Brand, current Connecticut governor Claire Debella, cutting-edge scientist Lionel Toussaint, fashion designer and former model Birdie Jay and her conscientious assistant Peg, and influencer Duke Cody and his sidekick girlfriend Whiskey. As in all the best murder mysteries, each character harbors their own secrets, lies and motivations. When someone turns up dead, everyone is a suspect.
